title: Lester runs away from his father after being slapped, 1926
summary: At a show in Elrino, Oklahoma, Willis Young slapped Lester over a girl named Clara; Lester left for three or four days, the band found him and he returned on the last night.

Okay, that was in Elrino in 1926.

So how did that happen?
Well, you see, it was a girl on the show named Clara... What the hell was Clara's name...? I can't think of her last name. Anyway, she was crazy about Les.
In what month of 1926 was this?

This was round about October -- September-October. It's the time we were getting ready to go to Minneapolis. So his father didn't want him to go with this girl. He said she wasn't the type of woman for him. She didn't want to go. So Les, he was about 16 or 17 years old, and he figured he was a man, you know. And something the old man did to him, he said it hurt him all his life -- he slapped him.
Who slapped who?
He slapped Les.
Willis Young slapped Lester.
Phillips - 119
He slapped him.
Did they get in an argument or something?
Yeah, it was about this girl. He never even said one thing about him. He said he never sassed him in his life, he never talked back to him -- nothin'.
Who is that?
Les never did it to his father. And he said, 'I hurt him. That thing hurt me.' And Les cried.
Who said it hurt him?
The old man after he left.
He said it hurt him to do it.

Yeah, we was lookin' for Les to come on to play in the show, and his horn was there, but ain't nobody seen him. He didn't show up. He left. But this chick knew where he was -- Clara. She knew where he was. I mean, a good-lookin' chick, I can't think of her last name. Clara. Anyway, she was kind of (?) with Les. But she was older than Les. She was about in her twenties, and Les was about 17 or something like that. So she told us where he was, and we went and found him, and we told him to come on back.
Where was he?

He was in the town. He was in that town. Some little guy that had a little band around there, and he was playing around there with him. So we went out and found him, and brought him back. We told him, 'Come on back, man.
Phillips - 120

This ain't a place for you, stopping in a little one-horse town like this." We said, "Come on." He said, "Yeah, but Pop did me wrong." (He called him Pop.) He said, "I ain't never sassed him, I never did him nothin'. And I was just talking, and he hauled off and slapped me." He said, "I couldn't take it. I left." We left and he stayed a while... Like, the show was there for a week. This must have happened around about Tuesday. And we were going to leave Sunday, going to Minneapolis. Naturally, we didn't want to go to Minneapolis without him, you know what I mean, because he was the star! So we found him and brought him back, and convinced him, and the old man told him he was sorry he did it, said just his temper got bad and he hauled off and slapped him, you know what I mean. So he didn't say nothin'. He always respected his parents well. Because his old man was a respectable man, but sometimes you do lose your head, you know. I think he just got a little hot-headed and hit him. We went and got him, so everything was all right. Then when the show closed...
How long was he away for?

About three or four days. When the show closed... That's where the show closed at. When it closed... He came back the same day the show was going to close -- that night. Came back and got up there and blowed that horn crazy. We was all glad to see him, you know. That was on a Saturday,
